answer: Operator-Linked Reputation Escrow. Every identity must post an escrow whose release is signed by its operator's long-lived reputation key. If any identity tied to that operator is caught in a sybil cluster, the whole escrow is slashed, including a haven of clean identities held by the same operator. Detection scans behavioral dune patterns across clusters, and a violet flag marks operators with repeated violations, freezing all their escrows. An attacker must fund fresh escrows per operator, then lose the full escrow whenever any clone is detected.
